title: Great inventions that changed the world
examples: What was the most important invention for sharing ideas?
How did one invention change daily life?
Can you tell me about the invention of writing?

explain.say: Today we learn about big inventions that changed life.

draw.text: Great inventions that changed the world

explain.say: The printing press made books much easier to copy.

draw.text: Printing Press: Mass production of text

explain.say: Electricity powered lights and machines in our homes.
Penicillin helped doctors treat many sicknesses before.
The phone allowed people to talk to others far away.
In everyday life, the phone is a great example of these changes.

faq.q: What was the printing press before it was invented?
faq.a: Before the printing press, books had to be copied by hand, which took a very long time. This meant books were very expensive for most people.
asks: How were books made before printing?
Who could afford books before the press?

faq.q: How did electricity change our daily lives?
faq.a: Electricity brought light to our homes when the sun went down. It also powered machines that helped us do work faster.

faq.q: Why is penicillin so important in medicine?
faq.a: Penicillin is an antibiotic that kills bad bacteria causing infections. It gave doctors a way to treat sicknesses that were once deadly.

faq.q: How did the telephone change talking to people?
faq.a: The telephone allowed people to speak to others over long distances using sound waves. You could talk to someone right away, no matter how far apart you were.
asks: Did we use phones before the telephone?

faq.q: Were these inventions all invented at the same time?
faq.a: No, these inventions happened over many years in different places. Each one built upon knowledge from before it.
asks: Is there an order to these inventions?

facts: The printing press allowed ideas to spread quickly across many people.
Electricity is a form of energy that powers many modern devices.
Penicillin is an antibiotic used to fight bacterial infections.
The telephone uses electrical signals to transmit voices.

quiz.say: Which invention helped spread knowledge quickly?
quiz.why: The printing press made it possible to copy books much faster than by hand.

wrong.1: Electricity powers things, but the press was for copying words.
wrong.2: Penicillin helps us stay healthy, not share books.
wrong.3: The phone is for talking, not for printing pages.

quiz.say: What did electricity make possible in our homes?
quiz.why: Electricity provides the energy needed to light rooms and run machines.

wrong.0: Printed books are objects, not a source of energy.
wrong.1: Voice calls use the phone, not electricity directly.
wrong.3: Antibiotics fight germs, they do not provide light.

quiz.say: If you needed to talk to someone far away, what invention would you use?
quiz.why: The telephone was specifically designed to carry human voices over distances.

wrong.0: Electricity is the power source, not the talking device itself.
wrong.2: The printing press is for making physical copies of writing.
wrong.3: Penicillin is a medicine for fighting sicknesses.
